title: Massacre at Parol and Kathuha (Chhota Ghallughara)

blocks.text: Dohra:
Parol, Kathuha and Basohli1 , were the towns, Situated were these in the district of Jammu. Was there a massacre on a large scale, Which took place at all these three places. (1)
lines: Parol,
Kathuha and Basohli1 , were the towns,
Situated were these in the district of Jammu.
Was there a massacre on a large scale,
Which took place at all these three places.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Since the day Jaspat Rai was slaughtered by the Singhs, No longer did they remain paupers and destitutes. Not only was the city of Emnabad destroyed, It was thoroughly ransacked by the Khalsa as well. (2)
lines: Since the day Jaspat Rai was slaughtered by the Singhs,
No longer did they remain paupers and destitutes.
Not only was the city of Emnabad destroyed,
It was thoroughly ransacked by the Khalsa as well.

blocks.text: A lot of treasure that was in possession of Jaspat Rai, Did the impoverished Singhs lay their hands upon. Thus becoming richer than the richest monarchs, Did the Singhs not care a fig for other monarchs. (3)
lines: A lot of treasure that was in possession of Jaspat Rai,
Did the impoverished Singhs lay their hands upon.
Thus becoming richer than the richest monarchs,
Did the Singhs not care a fig for other monarchs.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Hearing the news of Singhs' slaughter of (his brother) Jaspat Rai, Did Lakhpat Rai place his turban at the Nawab's feet. His turban would he put on his head only after, He had decimated the Khalsa Panth of Singhs. (4)
lines: Hearing the news of Singhs' slaughter of (his brother) Jaspat Rai,
Did Lakhpat Rai place his turban at the Nawab's feet.
His turban would he put on his head only after,
He had decimated the Khalsa Panth of Singhs.

blocks.text: Chaupai:
Making a solemn vow to liquidate the Singhs, Did he determine to invade and kill them instantly. Hearing this solemn resolution of Lakhpat Rai, Did the Nawab offer to fund his entire mission. (5)
lines: Making a solemn vow to liquidate the Singhs,
Did he determine to invade and kill them instantly.
Hearing this solemn resolution of Lakhpat Rai,
Did the Nawab offer to fund his entire mission.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Branding the Khalsa Panth as a good-for-nothing sect, Was it the creation of one of the Kashtriyas (Guru Nanak). Vowing himself to be worthy of being called a Kshtriya, Only after he had converted the Khalsa Panth into Islam. (6)
lines: Branding the Khalsa Panth as a good-for-nothing sect,
Was it the creation of one of the Kashtriyas (Guru Nanak).
Vowing himself to be worthy of being called a Kshtriya,
Only after he had converted the Khalsa Panth into Islam.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

This Sham organization was created by a Kashtriya, Which came to be known as the Khalsa Panth in the world. He vowed to claim himself to be Kshtriya, Only after had he liquidated the Khalsa Panth. (7)
lines: This Sham organization was created by a Kashtriya,
Which came to be known as the Khalsa Panth in the world.
He vowed to claim himself to be Kshtriya,
Only after had he liquidated the Khalsa Panth.

blocks.text: Thus did he boast of his arrogant bravado, Of which the Nawab did approve and support. Making Lakhpat Rai the commander of Mughal troops, Did the Nawab place all the troops under his command. (8)
lines: Thus did he boast of his arrogant bravado,
Of which the Nawab did approve and support.
Making Lakhpat Rai the commander of Mughal troops,
Did the Nawab place all the troops under his command.

blocks.text: Thus entering into collaboration with the Nawab, Did Lakhpat Rai vow to eliminate the Singhs everywhere. Let anyone claim himself to be called a Singh, Would Lakhpat Rai destroy whole of his village. (9)
lines: Thus entering into collaboration with the Nawab,
Did Lakhpat Rai vow to eliminate the Singhs everywhere.
Let anyone claim himself to be called a Singh,
Would Lakhpat Rai destroy whole of his village.

blocks.text: Dohra:
In the first attempt did he arrest those Singhs, Who had been in service as officials of the state. Handing them over to the state executioners, He ordered them to behead those Sikh officials. (10)
lines: In the first attempt did he arrest those Singhs,
Who had been in service as officials of the state.
Handing them over to the state executioners,
He ordered them to behead those Sikh officials.

blocks.text: Chaupai:
Hearing about such orders having been passed, Was there a lot of hue and cry among the populace. Organizing themselves into a joint deputation, Did all the Hindus approach Lakhpat Rai. (11)
lines: Hearing about such orders having been passed,
Was there a lot of hue and cry among the populace.
Organizing themselves into a joint deputation,
Did all the Hindus approach Lakhpat Rai.

blocks.text: Beseeching him to desist from executing Sikh officials, As they had no hand whatsoever in any criminal activity. Claiming to approach him on behalf of those innocents, Did they plead for forgiveness to those innocent Sikh officials. (12)
lines: Beseeching him to desist from executing Sikh officials,
As they had no hand whatsoever in any criminal activity.
Claiming to approach him on behalf of those innocents,
Did they plead for forgiveness to those innocent Sikh officials.

blocks.text: Having been approached by all the brothers from his Kshtriya fraternity, Dewan Lakhpat Rai must heed to their sane advice. The Kshtriya delegation including Kaura Mai2 and Kunjahi Mai, Also had Kashmiri Mai as one of its members. (13)
lines: Having been approached by all the brothers from his Kshtriya fraternity,
Dewan Lakhpat Rai must heed to their sane advice.
The Kshtriya delegation including Kaura Mai2 and Kunjahi Mai,
Also had Kashmiri Mai as one of its members.

blocks.text: It also included Lachhi Ram, the chief among the Dewans, Who was held in high esteem by the whole kshtriya fraternity. Approaching Jaspat Rai, did they plead for mercy to the Sikh officials, Their appeal being backed by Dewan Surat Singh. (14)
lines: It also included Lachhi Ram, the chief among the Dewans,
Who was held in high esteem by the whole kshtriya fraternity.
Approaching Jaspat Rai, did they plead for mercy to the Sikh officials,
Their appeal being backed by Dewan Surat Singh.

blocks.text: Dohra:

The delegation also included Dilay Ram and Hari Mai, As well as Behloo Mai who also joined. Hari Singh and Gulzar Singh too joined the delegation, Along with Bhai Des Raj (from the Lahore province). (15)
lines: The delegation also included Dilay Ram and Hari Mai,
As well as Behloo Mai who also joined.
Hari Singh and Gulzar Singh too joined the delegation,
Along with Bhai Des Raj (from the Lahore province).

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Beside these, most of the Hindus joined the delegation, Along with the Sikh saints and their devout followers. All of them pleaded with one voice for mercy, That the Sikh officials be released for the sake of all the Hindus. (16)
lines: Beside these, most of the Hindus joined the delegation,
Along with the Sikh saints and their devout followers.
All of them pleaded with one voice for mercy,
That the Sikh officials be released for the sake of all the Hindus.

blocks.text: All other people pleaded to Lakhpat Rai for God's sake, Including the saintly mendicants and those belonging to ascetic orders. Lakhpat Rai rejected the appeals of all these well meaning people, Of such an evil and obdurate disposition was he made of. (17)
lines: All other people pleaded to Lakhpat Rai for God's sake,
Including the saintly mendicants and those belonging to ascetic orders.
Lakhpat Rai rejected the appeals of all these well meaning people,
Of such an evil and obdurate disposition was he made of.

blocks.text: Reiterating that would he never budge an inch from his stand, Even if God Himself approached him for mercy. Thereupon, did the whole Kshtriya fraternity declare vociferously, Truly were the Singhs justified in killing his brother. (18)
lines: Reiterating that would he never budge an inch from his stand,
Even if God Himself approached him for mercy.
Thereupon, did the whole Kshtriya fraternity declare vociferously,
Truly were the Singhs justified in killing his brother.

blocks.text: Being instrumental in getting Bhai Mani Singh arrested and slaughtered, Truly had his brother received retribution for his evil deed. While majority of the Kshtriyas departed cursing him, Some of the elders did stay behind with Lakhpat Rai. (19)
lines: Being instrumental in getting Bhai Mani Singh arrested and slaughtered,
Truly had his brother received retribution for his evil deed.
While majority of the Kshtriyas departed cursing him,
Some of the elders did stay behind with Lakhpat Rai.

blocks.text: Dohra:

With folded hands did these Venerable elders plead, That Lakhpat should atleast grant them this little concession. That day being the auspicious day of Somvati Amavas3 , He should do what he intended to do on the next day. (20)
lines: With folded hands did these Venerable elders plead,
That Lakhpat should atleast grant them this little concession.
That day being the auspicious day of Somvati Amavas3 ,
He should do what he intended to do on the next day.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Refusing the elders to grant even this little concession, Did this obdurate ignorant autocrat execute the Sikh officials. Getting his royal proclamation announced in the city, Did he prohibit the worship of the Sikh Gurus. (21)
lines: Refusing the elders to grant even this little concession,
Did this obdurate ignorant autocrat execute the Sikh officials.
Getting his royal proclamation announced in the city,
Did he prohibit the worship of the Sikh Gurus.

blocks.text: If ever did he hear any of the Sikh Guru's name, Would he not spare the life of any such offender. Having prohibited the recitation of Sikh Guru's hymns, Did the Guru's followers proceed to conceal the sacred texts. (22)
lines: If ever did he hear any of the Sikh Guru's name,
Would he not spare the life of any such offender.
Having prohibited the recitation of Sikh Guru's hymns,
Did the Guru's followers proceed to conceal the sacred texts.

blocks.text: If ever did anyone recite the Sikh Guru's name, Would he single him out and convert him to Islam. Reiterating to wipe out the Sikh epithet "Waheguru" for God, Would he encourage the recitation of all other Divine names. (23)
lines: If ever did anyone recite the Sikh Guru's name,
Would he single him out and convert him to Islam.
Reiterating to wipe out the Sikh epithet "Waheguru" for God,
Would he encourage the recitation of all other Divine names.

blocks.text: Dohra:

A grocer's usage "Gurd"4 for jaggery being coterminus with "Gur", Did Lakhpat order grocers to change its name to "Rordi", If ever did anyone address anyone else naming him "Gur", Would he invade and raze his whole village to dust. (24)
lines: A grocer's usage "Gurd"4 for jaggery being coterminus with "Gur",
Did Lakhpat order grocers to change its name to "Rordi",
If ever did anyone address anyone else naming him "Gur",
Would he invade and raze his whole village to dust.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Such a havoc did Lakhpat Rai create thereafter, That he invaded the Khalsa forces (with a vengeance). Equipping his troops with cannons and small fire arms, He got those weapons fired at the Khalsa Panth troops. (25)
lines: Such a havoc did Lakhpat Rai create thereafter,
That he invaded the Khalsa forces (with a vengeance).
Equipping his troops with cannons and small fire arms,
He got those weapons fired at the Khalsa Panth troops.

blocks.text: Ordering his horse, elephant mounted and foot-soldiers to invade, He also made the general populace to follow the troops. Thereafter, the Mughal Nawab sent such written dispatches, That those who professed allegiance to him should support the Dewan. (26)
lines: Ordering his horse, elephant mounted and foot-soldiers to invade,
He also made the general populace to follow the troops.
Thereafter, the Mughal Nawab sent such written dispatches,
That those who professed allegiance to him should support the Dewan.

blocks.text: Alerting the Mughal troops deployed upto Multan5 and Bahawalpur, Did the Nawab order his troops to invade the Singhs. This included the troops deployed upto Kasur and Attock, As well as the troops stationed in the Doab triangle6 . (27)
lines: Alerting the Mughal troops deployed upto Multan5 and Bahawalpur,
Did the Nawab order his troops to invade the Singhs.
This included the troops deployed upto Kasur and Attock,
As well as the troops stationed in the Doab triangle6 .

blocks.text: Despatching the state messengers to all the hill chiefs, Did the Nawab summon them through very stern orders. He told them not to keep any active soldier at home, As he would not spare his life who shirked his duty. (28)
lines: Despatching the state messengers to all the hill chiefs,
Did the Nawab summon them through very stern orders.
He told them not to keep any active soldier at home,
As he would not spare his life who shirked his duty.

blocks.text: So stern being the orders of the Mughal Nawab, Who could dare to defy his royal proclamation? As nobody could dare to disobey his orders, All the people wished to run for the Singhs lives. (29)
lines: So stern being the orders of the Mughal Nawab,
Who could dare to defy his royal proclamation?
As nobody could dare to disobey his orders,
All the people wished to run for the Singhs lives.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Whosoever paid a visit to Dewan Lakhpat Rai, By way of mourning the death of Jaspat Rai. Such a visitor would also join the ranks of deceased Jaspat, As he would never be allowed to return home alive. (30)
lines: Whosoever paid a visit to Dewan Lakhpat Rai,
By way of mourning the death of Jaspat Rai.
Such a visitor would also join the ranks of deceased Jaspat,
As he would never be allowed to return home alive.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Making fresh recruitment to his Mughal army, Everyone was recruited whosoever came to be enlisted. Boasting of overpowering Singhs in a couple of days, Would he rest only after his mission was completed. (31)
lines: Making fresh recruitment to his Mughal army,
Everyone was recruited whosoever came to be enlisted.
Boasting of overpowering Singhs in a couple of days,
Would he rest only after his mission was completed.

blocks.text: As the Dewan Lakhpat Rai mounted his elephant, Even the sun seemed to be eclipsed with war's dust and din. Such indeed did the din and noise rise in the whole region, That no where could the Khalsa be allowed to take shelter. (32)
lines: As the Dewan Lakhpat Rai mounted his elephant,
Even the sun seemed to be eclipsed with war's dust and din.
Such indeed did the din and noise rise in the whole region,
That no where could the Khalsa be allowed to take shelter.

blocks.text: Appearing to uproot the Khalsa root and branch, Did the incensed Nawab proceed to avenge his brother's death. As do the dry leaves fly before a raging storm, So did the Singhs run for shelter ahead of Mughal invasion. (33)
lines: Appearing to uproot the Khalsa root and branch,
Did the incensed Nawab proceed to avenge his brother's death.
As do the dry leaves fly before a raging storm,
So did the Singhs run for shelter ahead of Mughal invasion.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Those who had joined the Singhs for instant favours, Instantly did they desert the Singhs ranks and went home. Those who had reposed their faith in their Guru, Did they stick to their mission, being firm in faith. (34)
lines: Those who had joined the Singhs for instant favours,
Instantly did they desert the Singhs ranks and went home.
Those who had reposed their faith in their Guru,
Did they stick to their mission, being firm in faith.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

As this information about war spread among the populace, So did the Mughal forces went in hot pursuit of Singhs. Many parents being concerned about their sons' safety, Did bring back their progeny home (through persuasions). (35)
lines: As this information about war spread among the populace,
So did the Mughal forces went in hot pursuit of Singhs.
Many parents being concerned about their sons' safety,
Did bring back their progeny home (through persuasions).

blocks.text: Many parents rushed to bring such youth home, As had joined the Singh ranks for robbing and plundering. Beseeching their sons to return home for safety, Their (desperate) mothers asked them to have their hair shorn. (36)
lines: Many parents rushed to bring such youth home,
As had joined the Singh ranks for robbing and plundering.
Beseeching their sons to return home for safety,
Their (desperate) mothers asked them to have their hair shorn.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Steadfast remained those who by their faith did abide, Deserted all those who in their faith did waver. To the heavens did their souls go who had sacrificed, Sovereigns of the land did they become who survived. (37)
lines: Steadfast remained those who by their faith did abide,
Deserted all those who in their faith did waver.
To the heavens did their souls go who had sacrificed,
Sovereigns of the land did they become who survived.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Stood their ground those alone as were the true Khalsa Singhs, When a direct confrontation took place between the two combatants. Though Singhs strength was as insignificant as a pinch of salt in a heap of flour, Yet they were as visible among Mughals as a spark of lightening among dark clouds. (38)
lines: Stood their ground those alone as were the true Khalsa Singhs,
When a direct confrontation took place between the two combatants.
Though Singhs strength was as insignificant as a pinch of salt in a heap of flour,
Yet they were as visible among Mughals as a spark of lightening among dark clouds.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Reckoning the strength of Mughal forces to be large in number, The Khalsa Singhs did assemble in a religious congregation. How should the Khalsa fight with the Mughal troops, As they had launched an invasion in their largest strength. (39)
lines: Reckoning the strength of Mughal forces to be large in number,
The Khalsa Singhs did assemble in a religious congregation.
How should the Khalsa fight with the Mughal troops,
As they had launched an invasion in their largest strength.

blocks.text: Those being hot-headed and brave among the Singhs, Did they vote for an instant spat with the Mughals. Those being seasoned and battle-hardened veterans, Did they advise to adopt a hit and run strategy. (40)
lines: Those being hot-headed and brave among the Singhs,
Did they vote for an instant spat with the Mughals.
Those being seasoned and battle-hardened veterans,
Did they advise to adopt a hit and run strategy.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Rightly had the elders narrated a war strategy, That hit and run indeed was the best kind of battle. Confrontation and desertion being equally valid strategies, Fight or perish were indeed half as good as hit and run. (41)
lines: Rightly had the elders narrated a war strategy,
That hit and run indeed was the best kind of battle.
Confrontation and desertion being equally valid strategies,
Fight or perish were indeed half as good as hit and run.

blocks.text: Opportunate desertion being approved by the Guru as a good strategy, Hit and run strategy indeed was the best policy. Guru himself having deserted the field while battling, Was there indeed nothing sinful about hitting and running. (42)
lines: Opportunate desertion being approved by the Guru as a good strategy,
Hit and run strategy indeed was the best policy.
Guru himself having deserted the field while battling,
Was there indeed nothing sinful about hitting and running.

blocks.text: Many a time did Lord Krishna7 desert the field of battle, In the mid-ocean he had to sit for protection. Pandavas8 to had to run away to save their lives, Seeking protection inside the Lakhi temple under-construction. (43)
lines: Many a time did Lord Krishna7 desert the field of battle,
In the mid-ocean he had to sit for protection.
Pandavas8 to had to run away to save their lives,
Seeking protection inside the Lakhi temple under-construction.

blocks.text: Dohra:

As advised by elderly veterans among the Khalsa Panth, The brave Singh warriors did obey their sane advice. Hitting and running did they proceed further, Taking shelter among the wilds (as and when required). (44)
lines: As advised by elderly veterans among the Khalsa Panth,
The brave Singh warriors did obey their sane advice.
Hitting and running did they proceed further,
Taking shelter among the wilds (as and when required).

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Thereafter, making a good use of a favourable opportunity, Did the Singhs slaughter the Mughal troops leading from the front. Thereupon feeling concerned at such a colossal loss of life, Did Dewan (Lakhpat Rai) attribute this loss to the lack of strategy. (45)
lines: Thereafter, making a good use of a favourable opportunity,
Did the Singhs slaughter the Mughal troops leading from the front.
Thereupon feeling concerned at such a colossal loss of life,
Did Dewan (Lakhpat Rai) attribute this loss to the lack of strategy.

blocks.text: Adopting an alternative strategy of troop deployment of his forces, He decided to deploy horse-mounted cannons in the front. Supporting this cavalry column by hand-operated guns from behind, He deployed a full column of small fire-arms wielding soldiers. (46)
lines: Adopting an alternative strategy of troop deployment of his forces,
He decided to deploy horse-mounted cannons in the front.
Supporting this cavalry column by hand-operated guns from behind,
He deployed a full column of small fire-arms wielding soldiers.

blocks.text: Deploying the columns of foot-soldiers at the rear end of his army, He kept the real striking force under his own command. Thus, turning the whole professional strategy topsy-turvy, Dewan Lakhpat, being scared of Singhs, himself remained in the rear. (47)
lines: Deploying the columns of foot-soldiers at the rear end of his army,
He kept the real striking force under his own command.
Thus, turning the whole professional strategy topsy-turvy,
Dewan Lakhpat, being scared of Singhs, himself remained in the rear.

blocks.text: As and when the running Singhs returned to hit the Mughals, They found themselves helpless in the face of canon fire. Being helpless, would the Singhs return to enter the wilds, Such being the ordeal confronting the Khalsa Panth. (48)
lines: As and when the running Singhs returned to hit the Mughals,
They found themselves helpless in the face of canon fire.
Being helpless, would the Singhs return to enter the wilds,
Such being the ordeal confronting the Khalsa Panth.

blocks.text: Beyond the cannon's range, would the Singhs retreat into the wilds, But little could they do to escape the attack from the Mughal cavalry. Would the Singhs kill those who got separated from the main army, Thus did the Singhs survive the ordeal many a time. (49)
lines: Beyond the cannon's range, would the Singhs retreat into the wilds,
But little could they do to escape the attack from the Mughal cavalry.
Would the Singhs kill those who got separated from the main army,
Thus did the Singhs survive the ordeal many a time.

blocks.text: Thereafter, summoning the forest guards (managing the forest), The Dewan made them layout footpaths through the thick forest. Setting on fire the thick bushes to make inroads, The guns were positioned to take aim at the Singhs. (50)
lines: Thereafter, summoning the forest guards (managing the forest),
The Dewan made them layout footpaths through the thick forest.
Setting on fire the thick bushes to make inroads,
The guns were positioned to take aim at the Singhs.

blocks.text: The Singhs being harassed and hounded to the extreme, Could not find anything to feed on and survive. Thus, being famished, did the Singhs retreat further, And emerged out of the wilds (being helpless). (51)
lines: The Singhs being harassed and hounded to the extreme,
Could not find anything to feed on and survive.
Thus, being famished, did the Singhs retreat further,
And emerged out of the wilds (being helpless).

blocks.text: Dohra:

While some took refuge in the wilds on this side of the river, Others hid themselves in the wilds on the other side of the river. Adopting such diverse tactics to save themselves, Did the Singhs carry on their march forward. (52)
lines: While some took refuge in the wilds on this side of the river,
Others hid themselves in the wilds on the other side of the river.
Adopting such diverse tactics to save themselves,
Did the Singhs carry on their march forward.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Reaching a point where the river Ravi could be swum across, Did the Singhs Swim through the river to reach the other bank. With the Singhs marching along the river's other bank, Were they chased and pursued by the Mughal forces. (53)
lines: Reaching a point where the river Ravi could be swum across,
Did the Singhs Swim through the river to reach the other bank.
With the Singhs marching along the river's other bank,
Were they chased and pursued by the Mughal forces.

blocks.text: Failing to put up a camp at any vantage point of safety, Did the Singhs continue their march day and night. Running short of every kind of provisions and equipment, How could they carry anything without any kind of carriage? (54)
lines: Failing to put up a camp at any vantage point of safety,
Did the Singhs continue their march day and night.
Running short of every kind of provisions and equipment,
How could they carry anything without any kind of carriage?

blocks.text: Having no access to any kind of arms and ammunition, How could the Singhs pick up a fight with the Mughal troops. Their weapons having been blunted with continuous usage, The Singhs too had gone without sleep for days together. (55)
lines: Having no access to any kind of arms and ammunition,
How could the Singhs pick up a fight with the Mughal troops.
Their weapons having been blunted with continuous usage,
The Singhs too had gone without sleep for days together.

blocks.text: The bows having been broken with a long use and wielding, They could get no more arrows to fill their quivers. Blades of their spears having remained struck in enemy's bodies, They could find no blacksmiths to sharpen their blades. (56)
lines: The bows having been broken with a long use and wielding,
They could get no more arrows to fill their quivers.
Blades of their spears having remained struck in enemy's bodies,
They could find no blacksmiths to sharpen their blades.

blocks.text: Their horses having become listless for want of proper feed, Their own bodies got sun burnt without proper clothing. Not to talk of any provisions in the form of food grains, Even potable drinking water became a scarce commodity. (57)
lines: Their horses having become listless for want of proper feed,
Their own bodies got sun burnt without proper clothing.
Not to talk of any provisions in the form of food grains,
Even potable drinking water became a scarce commodity.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Travelling (on foot) proverbially Known as partial death, Starvation is taken to be synonymous with (complete) death. Both these calamities having struck the Singhs together, These proved to be most catastrophic for the Khalsa Panth. (58)
lines: Travelling (on foot) proverbially Known as partial death,
Starvation is taken to be synonymous with (complete) death.
Both these calamities having struck the Singhs together,
These proved to be most catastrophic for the Khalsa Panth.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Having been stretched to the extreme with these calamities, The Singhs thought of seeking assistance from the Hindu brotherhood. Sneaking into the wilds on the slopes of hilly terrain, They expected to find some favours from their Hindu brethren. (59)
lines: Having been stretched to the extreme with these calamities,
The Singhs thought of seeking assistance from the Hindu brotherhood.
Sneaking into the wilds on the slopes of hilly terrain,
They expected to find some favours from their Hindu brethren.

blocks.text: For protection of the Hindus and decimation of the Mughals, Truly was the Khalsa Panth created (by the Divine Guru). Knowing little that these (hilly) Hindus being allies of the Mughals, They would certainly play foul with the Singhs. (60)
lines: For protection of the Hindus and decimation of the Mughals,
Truly was the Khalsa Panth created (by the Divine Guru).
Knowing little that these (hilly) Hindus being allies of the Mughals,
They would certainly play foul with the Singhs.

blocks.text: After having invited Banda Bahadur to lend them support, They had played a fraud with Banda Singh Bahadur. After Banda Bahadur had slaughtered the Mughals, They were instrumental in getting Banda Bahadur defeated. (61)
lines: After having invited Banda Bahadur to lend them support,
They had played a fraud with Banda Singh Bahadur.
After Banda Bahadur had slaughtered the Mughals,
They were instrumental in getting Banda Bahadur defeated.

blocks.text: Dohra:

The Singhs did not realize the hilly Hindu's treachery, That they had been traitors since the beginning. The Singhs had really forgotten (their past records), That they had handed over Banda Bahadur's followers to the Mughals. (62)
lines: The Singhs did not realize the hilly Hindu's treachery,
That they had been traitors since the beginning.
The Singhs had really forgotten (their past records),
That they had handed over Banda Bahadur's followers to the Mughals.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Thereafter, towards Basohali as the Singhs did proceed, They came across a large assembly of hilly people there. Expecting to receive a favourable response from them, Many Singhs proceeded to join the assembled Hindus. Instantly did the hilly Hindus slaughter the Singhs, While many of them were handed over to the Mughals. Instantly did the Mughals slaughter those captive Singhs, Such a catastrophe had struck the Singhs in this darkest moment. (64)
lines: Thereafter, towards Basohali as the Singhs did proceed,
They came across a large assembly of hilly people there.
Expecting to receive a favourable response from them,
Many Singhs proceeded to join the assembled Hindus.
Instantly did the hilly Hindus slaughter the Singhs,
While many of them were handed over to the Mughals.
Instantly did the Mughals slaughter those captive Singhs,
Such a catastrophe had struck the Singhs in this darkest moment.

blocks.text: Dohra:

In the like manner, those who had proceeded towards Parol and Kathuha, Those Singhs, too, had landed themselves in the snare. Having been robbed and demobbed by the Hindus, They ran for their lives repenting over their misadventure. (65)
lines: In the like manner, those who had proceeded towards Parol and Kathuha,
Those Singhs, too, had landed themselves in the snare.
Having been robbed and demobbed by the Hindus,
They ran for their lives repenting over their misadventure.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Thinking of taking a shelter among the mountains, The Singhs moved their camp towards the hilly heights. Noticing the mountainous range completely occupied by troops, They found hilly troops in full battle gear for war. (66)
lines: Thinking of taking a shelter among the mountains,
The Singhs moved their camp towards the hilly heights.
Noticing the mountainous range completely occupied by troops,
They found hilly troops in full battle gear for war.

blocks.text: Dohra:

These hill troops along with their respective hill chiefs, Had been summoned by the Nawab of Lahore. Seeing these hilly troops guarding the mountain tops, Did the Singhs feel concerned and threatened by them. (67)
lines: These hill troops along with their respective hill chiefs,
Had been summoned by the Nawab of Lahore.
Seeing these hilly troops guarding the mountain tops,
Did the Singhs feel concerned and threatened by them.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Thereafter, thinking of beating a hasty retreat for safety, Did the Singhs engage themselves in battling with the Mughal troops. Wielding their blunted swords in whatever side they could, Did the Singhs strike with a force to pierce through the enemy. (68)
lines: Thereafter, thinking of beating a hasty retreat for safety,
Did the Singhs engage themselves in battling with the Mughal troops.
Wielding their blunted swords in whatever side they could,
Did the Singhs strike with a force to pierce through the enemy.

blocks.text: If, perchance, blade of a spear got stuck inside enemy's body, Would the Singhs strike forcefully with a bare handle. Striking their adversary with a broken bow so strongly, The brave Singhs would rip apart the enemy's skull. (69)
lines: If, perchance, blade of a spear got stuck inside enemy's body,
Would the Singhs strike forcefully with a bare handle.
Striking their adversary with a broken bow so strongly,
The brave Singhs would rip apart the enemy's skull.

blocks.text: Hunting desperately for spotting out Lakhpat Rai, He could not be traced being hidden in the rear. The Bravest Singhs wherever they attacked with a sword, They chopped off the heads of their Mughal enemy. (70)
lines: Hunting desperately for spotting out Lakhpat Rai,
He could not be traced being hidden in the rear.
The Bravest Singhs wherever they attacked with a sword,
They chopped off the heads of their Mughal enemy.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Turning again and again they failed to make any dent, As the enemy had fortified their defences with cannons and muskets. Turning towards the river once again in desperation, They decided to cross the river somehow or the other. (71)
lines: Turning again and again they failed to make any dent,
As the enemy had fortified their defences with cannons and muskets.
Turning towards the river once again in desperation,
They decided to cross the river somehow or the other.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

As the Singhs stood on the river bank after beating a retreat, Was the river flowing in full torrent and flood. Resounding with the rise and fall of its tumultuous current, Were its waters gurgling with the formation of horrible whirlpools. (72)
lines: As the Singhs stood on the river bank after beating a retreat,
Was the river flowing in full torrent and flood.
Resounding with the rise and fall of its tumultuous current,
Were its waters gurgling with the formation of horrible whirlpools.

blocks.text: Flowing with its powerful resounding water current, It was uprooting many a tree standing on its banks. How could a human being dare to run through this current, Which was knocking down even the big boulders? (73)
lines: Flowing with its powerful resounding water current,
It was uprooting many a tree standing on its banks.
How could a human being dare to run through this current,
Which was knocking down even the big boulders?

blocks.text: Dohra:

Throwing an open challenge, the Khalsa Panth asked everyone, Could anyone of them measure the depth and flow of the current? So that all the Khalsa force could cross the river, Could anyone lead and pave the way through the current? (74)
lines: Throwing an open challenge, the Khalsa Panth asked everyone,
Could anyone of them measure the depth and flow of the current?
So that all the Khalsa force could cross the river,
Could anyone lead and pave the way through the current?

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Were there Singhs who had been inhabitants of Dalewal9 , Of being Kashtriya lineage were they four brothers. Appearing to be of a royal disposition and warrior like looks, Were they in possession of horses of fine exotic breed. (75)
lines: Were there Singhs who had been inhabitants of Dalewal9 ,
Of being Kashtriya lineage were they four brothers.
Appearing to be of a royal disposition and warrior like looks,
Were they in possession of horses of fine exotic breed.

blocks.text: Responding to the Khalsa' appeal two of them plunged into the river, Diving and emerging could they never come out. They were brothers of Gurdial Singh10 of Dalewal" , Whose name came to be associated with the Dalewal principality. (76)
lines: Responding to the Khalsa' appeal two of them plunged into the river,
Diving and emerging could they never come out.
They were brothers of Gurdial Singh10 of Dalewal" ,
Whose name came to be associated with the Dalewal principality.

blocks.text: Thereafter, did the Khalsa Panth come to the conclusion, That they were really confronted with a moment of extreme exigency. Better than getting drowned in the river one by one, Would it be much better to die killing ten others from the enemy ranks. (77)
lines: Thereafter, did the Khalsa Panth come to the conclusion,
That they were really confronted with a moment of extreme exigency.
Better than getting drowned in the river one by one,
Would it be much better to die killing ten others from the enemy ranks.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Thereafter, resolved the Khalsa after deep contemplation, That the moment of truth had indeed arrived. Truly had the revered Guru (Guru Gobind Singh) said, Standing in front of the Khalsa had he declared: (78)
lines: Thereafter, resolved the Khalsa after deep contemplation,
That the moment of truth had indeed arrived.
Truly had the revered Guru (Guru Gobind Singh) said,
Standing in front of the Khalsa had he declared:

blocks.text: "The (Sikh) warrior who dies fighting facing the enemy in battle, Would the Guru reckon him among the rarest of the rare warriors." Thereafter, giving up the plan to cross through the river, Did the Khalsa choose the sovereign way of fighting well. (79)
lines: "The (Sikh) warrior who dies fighting facing the enemy in battle,
Would the Guru reckon him among the rarest of the rare warriors." Thereafter, giving up the plan to cross through the river,
Did the Khalsa choose the sovereign way of fighting well.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Honouring the unanimous resolution of the Khalsa Panth, Did the Singhs obey the Khalsa Panth's dictat. Advancing in the four directions facing the enemy ranks, Did they never turn their faces from the formidable enemy. (80)
lines: Honouring the unanimous resolution of the Khalsa Panth,
Did the Singhs obey the Khalsa Panth's dictat.
Advancing in the four directions facing the enemy ranks,
Did they never turn their faces from the formidable enemy.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Those Singhs as were camping on the hill side, Did they make attempt to climb up the hills. But the hill troops column which guarded the hills, Did they not allow any passage of escape to the Singhs. (81)
lines: Those Singhs as were camping on the hill side,
Did they make attempt to climb up the hills.
But the hill troops column which guarded the hills,
Did they not allow any passage of escape to the Singhs.

blocks.text: Pelting a volley of stones, bricks and bullets from above, Their cannon balls hissed past the climbing Singhs. Ripping apart the Singh's bodies wherever these did hit, Were the enemy defences managed by Rajput soldiers. (82)
lines: Pelting a volley of stones, bricks and bullets from above,
Their cannon balls hissed past the climbing Singhs.
Ripping apart the Singh's bodies wherever these did hit,
Were the enemy defences managed by Rajput soldiers.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Nevertheless, exercising their utmost zeal and energy, The Singhs did succeed in capturing an enemy post. But the enemy soldiers being in far greater strength, Did they throw the Singhs back again from the captured post. (83)
lines: Nevertheless, exercising their utmost zeal and energy,
The Singhs did succeed in capturing an enemy post.
But the enemy soldiers being in far greater strength,
Did they throw the Singhs back again from the captured post.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Thereafter, making a fresh attempt (to consolidate themselves), Did the Singhs make a plan to climb up the mountains. For sheltering themselves in the foot hills of the mountains, Did the Singhs dig up trenches to shelter themselves. (84)
lines: Thereafter, making a fresh attempt (to consolidate themselves),
Did the Singhs make a plan to climb up the mountains.
For sheltering themselves in the foot hills of the mountains,
Did the Singhs dig up trenches to shelter themselves.

blocks.text: For keeping their heads out of the harm's way from above, Did the Singhs dig underground bunkers for their safety. Doing all this digging of earth with knives, daggers and small arms, Did the Singhs use spears, blades and swords for digging. (85)
lines: For keeping their heads out of the harm's way from above,
Did the Singhs dig underground bunkers for their safety.
Doing all this digging of earth with knives, daggers and small arms,
Did the Singhs use spears, blades and swords for digging.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Cutting step-ladders for stepping up the steep mountains, Did the Singhs push their way up with full force. Climbing up to the level of enemy held positions, Did the Singhs engage themselves in a fierce battle with the enemy. (86)
lines: Cutting step-ladders for stepping up the steep mountains,
Did the Singhs push their way up with full force.
Climbing up to the level of enemy held positions,
Did the Singhs engage themselves in a fierce battle with the enemy.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Thereupon, as the hill troops advanced amidst shouts, The Singhs, too, confronted them with full force. As the Singhs wielded their weapons upon the enemy, The hilly troops turned back after being hit. (87)
lines: Thereupon, as the hill troops advanced amidst shouts,
The Singhs, too, confronted them with full force.
As the Singhs wielded their weapons upon the enemy,
The hilly troops turned back after being hit.

blocks.text: Following the retreating hilly troops in hot pursuit, The Singh succeeded in wresting the hill feature from the enemy. While those on foot among the Singhs climbed up, Those on horses could they not go up the mountains. (88)
lines: Following the retreating hilly troops in hot pursuit,
The Singh succeeded in wresting the hill feature from the enemy.
While those on foot among the Singhs climbed up,
Those on horses could they not go up the mountains.

blocks.text: Thereupon, they located another passage to move, Which was to the lee side of the mountain towards the river. Cutting some earth with swords for making steps, They made their horses set their feet on those steps. (89)
lines: Thereupon, they located another passage to move,
Which was to the lee side of the mountain towards the river.
Cutting some earth with swords for making steps,
They made their horses set their feet on those steps.

blocks.text: With some surviving, some others stumbling on steps, The river drowned those who tumbled down the slopes. While those in the rear failed to join others in front, Everyone came under a siege wherever he was. (90)
lines: With some surviving, some others stumbling on steps,
The river drowned those who tumbled down the slopes.
While those in the rear failed to join others in front,
Everyone came under a siege wherever he was.

blocks.text: Neither could they find any room to march forward, Nor could they beat a retreat in anyway whatsoever. The narrow hilly passage getting overcrowed with them, Many drowned in the river who slipped and stumbled from above. (91)
lines: Neither could they find any room to march forward,
Nor could they beat a retreat in anyway whatsoever.
The narrow hilly passage getting overcrowed with them,
Many drowned in the river who slipped and stumbled from above.

blocks.text: Reckoning those in the rear to be at a vantage point, Those in the rear considered the front runners to be better placed. Without anybody suggesting any escape route to anybody else, The Singhs proceeded in whatever way each could find. (92)
lines: Reckoning those in the rear to be at a vantage point,
Those in the rear considered the front runners to be better placed.
Without anybody suggesting any escape route to anybody else,
The Singhs proceeded in whatever way each could find.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

What to think of feeding oneself with any foodstuff, It was impossible even to drink a drop of water. But with some mysterious power pushing their bodies, They did not stop their march with their grit and determination. (93)
lines: What to think of feeding oneself with any foodstuff,
It was impossible even to drink a drop of water.
But with some mysterious power pushing their bodies,
They did not stop their march with their grit and determination.

blocks.text: Having gone without food for many days together, Could the Singhs not get a morsel of bread even on begging. Instead the hill troops would rush to kill the Singhs, Or hand them over to the Mughals after putting them in fetters. (94)
lines: Having gone without food for many days together,
Could the Singhs not get a morsel of bread even on begging.
Instead the hill troops would rush to kill the Singhs,
Or hand them over to the Mughals after putting them in fetters.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Observing so much blood-letting, gore, killing and being killed, Did the Singh lose all sense of appetite and hunger. The famished Singhs had to content themselves perforce, By having a mere glimpse of the green trees on the hills. (95)
lines: Observing so much blood-letting, gore, killing and being killed,
Did the Singh lose all sense of appetite and hunger.
The famished Singhs had to content themselves perforce,
By having a mere glimpse of the green trees on the hills.

blocks.text: Those standing on hill tops kept perched there, Those standing at the foothills need to be described. Would I (the author) narrate the same account, As I had heard it described from my father. (96)
lines: Those standing on hill tops kept perched there,
Those standing at the foothills need to be described.
Would I (the author) narrate the same account,
As I had heard it described from my father.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

The Mughals stepped up their pressure on the Singhs in the foothills, As they reckoned the Singhs were about to desert. The Mughals launched an attack on the Singhs, With the blowing of a bugle instead of the drum beat. (97)
lines: The Mughals stepped up their pressure on the Singhs in the foothills,
As they reckoned the Singhs were about to desert.
The Mughals launched an attack on the Singhs,
With the blowing of a bugle instead of the drum beat.

blocks.text: Making a public proclamation through a court announcer, They prohibited the robbing of Singhs under siege. Putting a price on the head of each Sikh captive, They promised a payment of five rupees for each Sikh's head. (98)
lines: Making a public proclamation through a court announcer,
They prohibited the robbing of Singhs under siege.
Putting a price on the head of each Sikh captive,
They promised a payment of five rupees for each Sikh's head.

blocks.text: Lakhpat Rai promised to condone the robbing of Sikhs, Only after had all of them been slaughtered by Mughals. In case the public indulged in robbing before killing the Singhs, They might escape and sneak into the wilds. (99)
lines: Lakhpat Rai promised to condone the robbing of Sikhs,
Only after had all of them been slaughtered by Mughals.
In case the public indulged in robbing before killing the Singhs,
They might escape and sneak into the wilds.

blocks.text: After this order, did the Singhs come under a swear attack, As the Mughals attacked them with cannon fire and sword blows. Being kicked and crushed by the Mughal horses' hooves, The Singhs, too, picked up their weapons to combat the attack. (100)
lines: After this order, did the Singhs come under a swear attack,
As the Mughals attacked them with cannon fire and sword blows.
Being kicked and crushed by the Mughal horses' hooves,
The Singhs, too, picked up their weapons to combat the attack.

blocks.text: Recalling the Gurus' inspiring words (at the time of adversity), The Singhs made a thrust forward girding up their loins. After hitting the Singhs with horse's kicks and hooves, The Mughal force did make a hasty retreat. (101)
lines: Recalling the Gurus' inspiring words (at the time of adversity),
The Singhs made a thrust forward girding up their loins.
After hitting the Singhs with horse's kicks and hooves,
The Mughal force did make a hasty retreat.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Sukha Singh then made a (solemn) declaration, That he would make an attempt at Lakhpat Rai. He alone should accompany him (Sukha Singh) in this mission, Who would never withdraw his steps at any cost. (102)
lines: Sukha Singh then made a (solemn) declaration,
That he would make an attempt at Lakhpat Rai.
He alone should accompany him (Sukha Singh) in this mission,
Who would never withdraw his steps at any cost.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Therafter, sending a spy on intelligence gathering, Did he ask him to locate the whereabouts of Lakhpat Rai. Informing that it would be impossible to get at Lakhpat Rai, The spy informed about the heavy security cordon around him. (103)
lines: Therafter, sending a spy on intelligence gathering,
Did he ask him to locate the whereabouts of Lakhpat Rai.
Informing that it would be impossible to get at Lakhpat Rai,
The spy informed about the heavy security cordon around him.

blocks.text: Lakhpat Rai was seen to be mounted on a red-seated elephant, Where he sat majestically without an iota of fear. He kept on changing his locations on various elephants, Now mounting a horse and then sitting in a palanquin soon after. (104)
lines: Lakhpat Rai was seen to be mounted on a red-seated elephant,
Where he sat majestically without an iota of fear.
He kept on changing his locations on various elephants,
Now mounting a horse and then sitting in a palanquin soon after.

blocks.text: He kept himself surrounded by many foot soldiers, Who were further encircled by horse-mounted troops, Ahead of these, there was a column of camel-loaded guns, Beyond which were the cannons positioned systematically. (105)
lines: He kept himself surrounded by many foot soldiers,
Who were further encircled by horse-mounted troops,
Ahead of these, there was a column of camel-loaded guns,
Beyond which were the cannons positioned systematically.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Not getting deterred by the reports of top-heavy security, Sukha Singh did make an attempt at Lakhpat Rai. Being hit by a fire ball from a small cannon, One of his legs was ripped apart by a deadly hit. (106)
lines: Not getting deterred by the reports of top-heavy security,
Sukha Singh did make an attempt at Lakhpat Rai.
Being hit by a fire ball from a small cannon,
One of his legs was ripped apart by a deadly hit.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Getting crippled with an unbearable pain from a broken leg, He failed to accomplish his cherished desire. Strapping his seriously wounded leg to the horses' saddle, He could not muster his courage to proceed further. (107)
lines: Getting crippled with an unbearable pain from a broken leg,
He failed to accomplish his cherished desire.
Strapping his seriously wounded leg to the horses' saddle,
He could not muster his courage to proceed further.

blocks.text: Beating a retreat from where he was hit, He kept on returning and positioning to hit back, Refusing to disarm himself despite a grievous wound, He kept his morale high on the basis of his determination. (108)
lines: Beating a retreat from where he was hit,
He kept on returning and positioning to hit back,
Refusing to disarm himself despite a grievous wound,
He kept his morale high on the basis of his determination.

blocks.text: Wherever he found the Singhs in danger in the battlefield, Would he put himself in the highest danger. (Dear readers), listen further to the account of battle, That raged partly on the mountains, partly on the foothills. (109)
lines: Wherever he found the Singhs in danger in the battlefield,
Would he put himself in the highest danger.
(Dear readers), listen further to the account of battle,
That raged partly on the mountains, partly on the foothills.

blocks.text: Thereafter, the Khalsa Panth made a fresh resolution, That they would not be able to defeat the Mughals at that stage. The Mughals being in majority and the Singhs in minority, The Singhs and their horses too had been without food. (110)
lines: Thereafter, the Khalsa Panth made a fresh resolution,
That they would not be able to defeat the Mughals at that stage.
The Mughals being in majority and the Singhs in minority,
The Singhs and their horses too had been without food.

blocks.text: Now would the Khalsa Panth force desert the field, Would they certainly return with full preparation to deal with the Mughals. Must they escape for the present in all the four directions, They should bide the time by deserting for the time being. (Ill) Opportunate desertion as strategy having been taught by the Guru, Hitting and running tactics had also been included in it. Even Gods had been deserting the field against the demons, Recovering their territory from demons after some time. (112)
lines: Now would the Khalsa Panth force desert the field,
Would they certainly return with full preparation to deal with the Mughals.
Must they escape for the present in all the four directions,
They should bide the time by deserting for the time being.
(Ill) Opportunate desertion as strategy having been taught by the Guru,
Hitting and running tactics had also been included in it.
Even Gods had been deserting the field against the demons,
Recovering their territory from demons after some time.

blocks.text: Lord Krishna12 too had to run from the field many a time, Despite his being an incarnation of Lord Vishnu. Lord Shiva13 too had to run to escape demon Bhasmantar's blow. But destroying the demon later on after a gap of sometime. (113)
lines: Lord Krishna12 too had to run from the field many a time,
Despite his being an incarnation of Lord Vishnu.
Lord Shiva13 too had to run to escape demon Bhasmantar's blow.
But destroying the demon later on after a gap of sometime.

blocks.text: Dohra:
Sukha Singh who came from a family of carpenters, Was he a native of village Mari-Kambo-Ki14 . He would keep opposing Lakhpat Rai's movement, Leading a contingent of Singhs from the front. (114)
lines: Sukha Singh who came from a family of carpenters,
Was he a native of village Mari-Kambo-Ki14 .
He would keep opposing Lakhpat Rai's movement,
Leading a contingent of Singhs from the front.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Thereafter, the Khalsa Panth arrived at a resolution, That each one of them should try to protect himself. Those who were not able to come up the hill with their horses, They shouted in their loudest voices to their colleagues. (115)
lines: Thereafter, the Khalsa Panth arrived at a resolution,
That each one of them should try to protect himself.
Those who were not able to come up the hill with their horses,
They shouted in their loudest voices to their colleagues.

blocks.text: Since they could not climb the hill with their horses, They would better retreat to save their lives. As their horses could not climb up the steep hills, They would not be able to attack without their horses. (16)
lines: Since they could not climb the hill with their horses,
They would better retreat to save their lives.
As their horses could not climb up the steep hills,
They would not be able to attack without their horses.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Thereupon the Khalsa Panth made a loud declaration, That they must scatter themselves in all the directions. Thereafter, they should reassemble in the Majha region, To create havoc and anarchic conditions once again. (117)
lines: Thereupon the Khalsa Panth made a loud declaration,
That they must scatter themselves in all the directions.
Thereafter, they should reassemble in the Majha region,
To create havoc and anarchic conditions once again.

blocks.text: Chaupai:
Thereafter, Sukha Singh counseled the Singhs, That they must follow him from the backside. Whosoever was on foot among the Singh soldiers, He must climb up the hill without any loss of time. (118)
lines: Thereafter,
Sukha Singh counseled the Singhs,
That they must follow him from the backside.
Whosoever was on foot among the Singh soldiers,
He must climb up the hill without any loss of time.

blocks.text: Those mounted on their horses must follow them, In no case should they venture to climb up the hill. As long as those on foot kept climbing up the steep hill, Would those on horses keep providing them protection. (119)
lines: Those mounted on their horses must follow them,
In no case should they venture to climb up the hill.
As long as those on foot kept climbing up the steep hill,
Would those on horses keep providing them protection.

blocks.text: Dohra:

No sooner did Sukha Singh make a declaration, Counseling the Singhs to disperse for their personal safety, Then every father departed from his son, Even as a brother got separated from his brother. (120)
lines: No sooner did Sukha Singh make a declaration,
Counseling the Singhs to disperse for their personal safety,
Then every father departed from his son,
Even as a brother got separated from his brother.

blocks.text: After Sukha Singh had made an assessment, That all the Singh foot-soldiers had reached the hill top, His contingent endeavoured to cross through the river, By making some sort of improvised wooden boats. (121)
lines: After Sukha Singh had made an assessment,
That all the Singh foot-soldiers had reached the hill top,
His contingent endeavoured to cross through the river,
By making some sort of improvised wooden boats.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Thereafter, Sukha Singh again made a suggestion, That they must pounce upon Lakhpat Rai. Would that somebody could let him know his location, He (Sukha Singh) would either kill Lakhpat Rai or sacrifice his own life. (122)
lines: Thereafter,
Sukha Singh again made a suggestion,
That they must pounce upon Lakhpat Rai.
Would that somebody could let him know his location,
He (Sukha Singh) would either kill Lakhpat Rai or sacrifice his own life.

blocks.text: Thereupon, did the seasoned veterans proffer an advice, That the Singhs were not in a position to fight for the present. They must desert that place for the time being, Making the Malwa region as their next destination. (123)
lines: Thereupon, did the seasoned veterans proffer an advice,
That the Singhs were not in a position to fight for the present.
They must desert that place for the time being,
Making the Malwa region as their next destination.

blocks.text: Dohra:

There being positioned a large Mughal force in front, How could they cross through the Mughal column? So much with cannons and guns had the Mughals fortified the passage, That there was hardly any space to sneak through their defences. (124)
lines: There being positioned a large Mughal force in front,
How could they cross through the Mughal column?
So much with cannons and guns had the Mughals fortified the passage,
That there was hardly any space to sneak through their defences.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Someone suggested to find a passage for escape, Where there was less concentration of Mughal troops. Some other suggested to cross through the flooded river, Still another suggested to climb up the steep hill. (125)
lines: Someone suggested to find a passage for escape,
Where there was less concentration of Mughal troops.
Some other suggested to cross through the flooded river,
Still another suggested to climb up the steep hill.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Thereupon, Sukha Singh did make a declaration, They (Singhs) would never survive through stealth. Without coming into a direct confrontation with the Mughals, Had they not been left with any other alternative. (126)
lines: Thereupon,
Sukha Singh did make a declaration,
They (Singhs) would never survive through stealth.
Without coming into a direct confrontation with the Mughals,
Had they not been left with any other alternative.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Thereafter, Sukha Ssingh gave an open call to all the Sikhs, That the entire Khalsa Panth force should follow after him. Must the Singhs invade the strongest Mughal defences, Without caring for the safety of their own lives. (127)
lines: Thereafter,
Sukha Ssingh gave an open call to all the Sikhs,
That the entire Khalsa Panth force should follow after him.
Must the Singhs invade the strongest Mughal defences,
Without caring for the safety of their own lives.

blocks.text: After this boosting of morale by Sukha Singh, Did the Singhs attack the posts held by the enemy. The ones defending those posts ran away to far off places, Making way for the Singhs while fleeing from their posts. (128)
lines: After this boosting of morale by Sukha Singh,
Did the Singhs attack the posts held by the enemy.
The ones defending those posts ran away to far off places,
Making way for the Singhs while fleeing from their posts.

blocks.text: Those who resisted were they killed by the Singhs, As were they dispossessed of their weapons as well. After this, spotting out a wild growth ahead of them, Did Sukha Singh sneak into the wild. (129)
lines: Those who resisted were they killed by the Singhs,
As were they dispossessed of their weapons as well.
After this, spotting out a wild growth ahead of them,
Did Sukha Singh sneak into the wild.

blocks.text: The direction in which had Sukha Singh proceeded, Did majority of Singhs proceed in the self-same direction. But soon did the Mughal troops converge from both the sides, Who had been following the Singhs in hot pursuit. (130)
lines: The direction in which had Sukha Singh proceeded,
Did majority of Singhs proceed in the self-same direction.
But soon did the Mughal troops converge from both the sides,
Who had been following the Singhs in hot pursuit.

blocks.text: Opening a volley of cannon fire from both the Mughal flanks, Did the Mughals rush to attack the besieged Singhs. Firing cannon balls at the Singhs from both the sides, Did the Mughals start slaughtering the encircled Singhs. (131)
lines: Opening a volley of cannon fire from both the Mughal flanks,
Did the Mughals rush to attack the besieged Singhs.
Firing cannon balls at the Singhs from both the sides,
Did the Mughals start slaughtering the encircled Singhs.

blocks.text: The Singhs who proceeded in a group together, They did escape while hitting at the Mughal troops. Those who got separated in the rear guard, Were they killed by the Mughals in a combined lot. (132)
lines: The Singhs who proceeded in a group together,
They did escape while hitting at the Mughal troops.
Those who got separated in the rear guard,
Were they killed by the Mughals in a combined lot.

blocks.text: Would Sukha Singh halt and wait for others to join, But little could Singhs resist being out numbered in strength. Fighting and resisting as the Singhs did enter the wild, The Mughals, too, did keep their chase in the jungle. (133)
lines: Would Sukha Singh halt and wait for others to join,
But little could Singhs resist being out numbered in strength.
Fighting and resisting as the Singhs did enter the wild,
The Mughals, too, did keep their chase in the jungle.

blocks.text: Whosoever among the Singhs fell into the Mughal's hands, Did the Mughals despatch him to death in an instant. The Singhs who had proceeded towards the wild, Would Rattan Singh narrate how it passed with them. (134)
lines: Whosoever among the Singhs fell into the Mughal's hands,
Did the Mughals despatch him to death in an instant.
The Singhs who had proceeded towards the wild,
Would Rattan Singh narrate how it passed with them.

blocks.text: Darkness did descend as did the Singhs enter the wild, So did the Mughal troops return to their base camp. Thus did the Singhs get a (temporary) shelter in the wild, Thus did they cool their nerves after a bout of loot and fight. (135)
lines: Darkness did descend as did the Singhs enter the wild,
So did the Mughal troops return to their base camp.
Thus did the Singhs get a (temporary) shelter in the wild,
Thus did they cool their nerves after a bout of loot and fight.

blocks.text: At midnight did the Singhs begin their march again, When they were again followed by the Mughal troops. As the Mughals were continuously hunting for the Singhs, They did kill those Singhs whom they found lying wounded. (136)
lines: At midnight did the Singhs begin their march again,
When they were again followed by the Mughal troops.
As the Mughals were continuously hunting for the Singhs,
They did kill those Singhs whom they found lying wounded.

blocks.text: Fatigued, famished and naked were Singhs rendered, Very few among them being up and moving. They were again surrounded by the Mughal troops, These emaciated Singhs started fighting once again. (137)
lines: Fatigued, famished and naked were Singhs rendered,
Very few among them being up and moving.
They were again surrounded by the Mughal troops,
These emaciated Singhs started fighting once again.

blocks.text: Whichever Mughal soldier dared to enter the wild, The Singhs did pounce upon him and killed him. Whichever Singh ventured to get out of the wild, The Mughals too did attack and despatch him to death. (138)
lines: Whichever Mughal soldier dared to enter the wild,
The Singhs did pounce upon him and killed him.
Whichever Singh ventured to get out of the wild,
The Mughals too did attack and despatch him to death.

blocks.text: Thereafter the Khalsa Singhs took another decision, That desertion and escape alone would not avail. They must keep hitting-running hitting again and again, Till they could reach a bigger patch of jungle for shelter. (139)
lines: Thereafter the Khalsa Singhs took another decision,
That desertion and escape alone would not avail.
They must keep hitting-running hitting again and again,
Till they could reach a bigger patch of jungle for shelter.

blocks.text: Dohra:
As the Singhs attempted to enter a smaller patch, Would the Mughal troops harass the Singhs a lot, But as the Singhs got into a bigger patch, Would the Singh kill the Mughals in large numbers. (140)
lines: As the Singhs attempted to enter a smaller patch,
Would the Mughal troops harass the Singhs a lot,
But as the Singhs got into a bigger patch,
Would the Singh kill the Mughals in large numbers.

blocks.text: Chaupai:
Thereafter, the Mughals decided upon another plan, That they must summon a large gathering of people. They must push this crowd into the jungle, Which would then eliminate all these Singhs. (141)
lines: Thereafter, the Mughals decided upon another plan,
That they must summon a large gathering of people.
They must push this crowd into the jungle,
Which would then eliminate all these Singhs.

blocks.text: Thereafter, as the Dewan called the public with a beat of drum, The public gathered there in response to this proclamation. As the Mughals pushed these subjects into the wild, They were armed with muskets and sharp spears. (142)
lines: Thereafter, as the Dewan called the public with a beat of drum,
The public gathered there in response to this proclamation.
As the Mughals pushed these subjects into the wild,
They were armed with muskets and sharp spears.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Thus did these subjects confront the Singhs, Adopting several kinds of tactics and maneavours. This intrusion did create a piquant situation, As the Singhs were at their wit's ends to deal with public. (143)
lines: Thus did these subjects confront the Singhs,
Adopting several kinds of tactics and maneavours.
This intrusion did create a piquant situation,
As the Singhs were at their wit's ends to deal with public.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Thereupon, did Sukha Singh make a declaration, That the Singhs had to kill the people for their own survival. They could stay in the wild in peace and safety, Only after they had done away with these intruders. (144)
lines: Thereupon, did Sukha Singh make a declaration,
That the Singhs had to kill the people for their own survival.
They could stay in the wild in peace and safety,
Only after they had done away with these intruders.

blocks.text: Would these civilian intruders eliminate the Singhs, In case the Singhs failed to get rid of these subjects. Thus did besieged Singhs survive with the daring of a burglar alone, As the Divine Satguru had ordained the Khalsa's survival. (145)
lines: Would these civilian intruders eliminate the Singhs,
In case the Singhs failed to get rid of these subjects.
Thus did besieged Singhs survive with the daring of a burglar alone,
As the Divine Satguru had ordained the Khalsa's survival.

blocks.text: Dohra:

As the Singhs rushed upon to pounce on the intruders, The Jat intruders started fleeing before them. As the Singhs robbed those whom they caught, They let many of those escape who chose to flee. (146)
lines: As the Singhs rushed upon to pounce on the intruders,
The Jat intruders started fleeing before them.
As the Singhs robbed those whom they caught,
They let many of those escape who chose to flee.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

The Singhs snatched the horses of many an intruder, While many others left their robes and weapons behind. Thus, did the Singhs proceed being well-equipped, Though the prominent warriors had all exhausted. (147)
lines: The Singhs snatched the horses of many an intruder,
While many others left their robes and weapons behind.
Thus, did the Singhs proceed being well-equipped,
Though the prominent warriors had all exhausted.

blocks.text: As the Singhs got a temporary relief from fighting, Did they decide to head for the Majha region. As the next immediate region belonged to wicked Rama Randhawa15 , Did the Singhs resolve to cross this region in a single night. (148)
lines: As the Singhs got a temporary relief from fighting,
Did they decide to head for the Majha region.
As the next immediate region belonged to wicked Rama Randhawa15 ,
Did the Singhs resolve to cross this region in a single night.

blocks.text: As the Singhs confabulated how to cross the river, Did they endeavour to wade through this river. Camping upon the river's bank under the searing heat at noon, Did the Singhs make make-shift boats of reeds and grass. (149)
lines: As the Singhs confabulated how to cross the river,
Did they endeavour to wade through this river.
Camping upon the river's bank under the searing heat at noon,
Did the Singhs make make-shift boats of reeds and grass.

blocks.text: As the Singhs waded through the river to the other bank, Did they take rest there for a few hours to relax. Thereafter, saddling the horses by tying their buckles, Did the Singhs launch on their march on an onward mission. ((150)
lines: As the Singhs waded through the river to the other bank,
Did they take rest there for a few hours to relax.
Thereafter, saddling the horses by tying their buckles,
Did the Singhs launch on their march on an onward mission.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Whatever equipage had the Singhs carried with them, It got drowned in water during their passage through the river. They got their feet scorched in the hot sands, As they had to walk through the sandy terrain barefooted. (151)
lines: Whatever equipage had the Singhs carried with them,
It got drowned in water during their passage through the river.
They got their feet scorched in the hot sands,
As they had to walk through the sandy terrain barefooted.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

So intensely hot and sandy was the river plateau, As if somebody had laid out a hot plate. The Singhs had to tear off their dresses to make footpads, So that they could protect their feet from being scorched. (152)
lines: So intensely hot and sandy was the river plateau,
As if somebody had laid out a hot plate.
The Singhs had to tear off their dresses to make footpads,
So that they could protect their feet from being scorched.

blocks.text: Dohra:

As the Singhs attempted to wrap up their feet in rags, They squatted on their haunches on the hot sand. As their bottoms got scorched by the hot sands, Did the Singhs let out a desperate cry in pain. (153)
lines: As the Singhs attempted to wrap up their feet in rags,
They squatted on their haunches on the hot sand.
As their bottoms got scorched by the hot sands,
Did the Singhs let out a desperate cry in pain.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Thus did the Singhs cross the riverine terrain, And finally sneaked into their (native) Majha region. Finally crossing at the confluence16 of both the rivers, The Singhs did reach the outskirts of (Lakhi) jungle. (154)
lines: Thus did the Singhs cross the riverine terrain,
And finally sneaked into their (native) Majha region.
Finally crossing at the confluence16 of both the rivers,
The Singhs did reach the outskirts of (Lakhi) jungle.

blocks.text: There being located a village by the name Jaito17 , The Singhs did put up a camp there for a while. There removing the bandage from the wounded leg, Sukha Singh got his fracture repaired by the experts. (155)
lines: There being located a village by the name Jaito17 ,
The Singhs did put up a camp there for a while.
There removing the bandage from the wounded leg,
Sukha Singh got his fracture repaired by the experts.

blocks.text: There putting the fractured leg in a pipe in a lubricated plaster, Sukha Singh had to rest in bed much against his wishes. Even with all the efforts of experts to repair the fracture, It took five to six months to heal the whole wound. (156)
lines: There putting the fractured leg in a pipe in a lubricated plaster,
Sukha Singh had to rest in bed much against his wishes.
Even with all the efforts of experts to repair the fracture,
It took five to six months to heal the whole wound.

blocks.text: Thereafter thorough ablutions did Sukha Singh wear his armour, Did he mount his horse again with the same missionary zeal. Thus had the author heard the whole account from his father, As his father had brought Sukha Singh home with him to his native place. (157)
lines: Thereafter thorough ablutions did Sukha Singh wear his armour,
Did he mount his horse again with the same missionary zeal.
Thus had the author heard the whole account from his father,
As his father had brought Sukha Singh home with him to his native place.
